rationale: The longer tart cherry concentrate comparison favors task-related mental fatigue. Acute ratings and a separate four-week rugby concentrate study are inconclusive. A cherry-cocoa report leaves the trial design and exertion comparator unverified. The lean against worsening remains minimal because the relevant comparisons used concentrates and fatigue measures outside Parkinson disease.

The Belem Parkinson cohort recorded watermelon intake without preparation or bradykinesia by intake. The animal studies use juice, isolated lycopene or a mixed seed extract and measure movement proxies. These studies leave the effect of raw watermelon on clinical bradykinesia unresolved.

An author preprint reports acute drooling after a mixed snack containing watermelon seed paste in a toddler who previously tolerated the flesh. The suspected allergy and seed preparation leave the raw-flesh and Parkinson drooling hypothesis unresolved.

COMBAT confirms baseline screening and provides no randomized post-treatment depression comparison. The cranberry drink and mixed-product altitude comparisons were inconclusive. The extract studies measured mouse behavior or enzyme activity, without a clinical mood outcome. The direction for dried cranberry and depressive symptoms in Parkinson disease remains unresolved.

The resting-pressure juice crossover and separate raw-flesh and ambulatory studies give mixed or inconclusive results. A dementia case places watermelon in a visual error and measures positional blood pressure without an assigned exposure. A comparison measuring standing lightheadedness after raw watermelon in Parkinson disease remains open.
